title: Geometry-Controlled Exciton Selectivity in Monolayer MoS2 Using Plasmonic Hollow Nanocavities
summary: Spectral control of closely spaced excitonic transitions is central to valleytronic photonics, nanoscale light sources, and wavelength-encoded sensing. In monolayer molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), the A and B excitons are separated by only tens of meV, making selective excitonic emission control both fundamentally important and technologically challenging. Here, we numerically investigate plasmon-enhanced excitonic emission from monolayer MoS2 coupled to vertically oriented hollow gold nanocylindrical cavities through a dielectric spacer.
